cards.text: Abraham has just welcomed visitors at his tent, and the LORD has promised that his wife Sarah will have a son (Genesis 18:1-15). When the men get up to leave, they look out over the city of Sodom, and Abraham walks along with them to see them off. These days most of us see a guest off by yelling "BYE" from the couch, so give this man some credit.
Then the LORD asks, "Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?" Friend, when you hear a line like THAT, you put the cookie down and you lean in.
The LORD says Abraham will surely become a great and powerful nation, and through him all the nations of the earth will be blessed. That's not a small promise, friend.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD says He chose Abraham so Abraham would command his children and his household to keep the way of the LORD by doing what is right and just.

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks about two cities, Sodom and Gomorrah. The outcry against them is great, and their sin is so grievous.

cards.question: With an outcry that great against Sodom and Gomorrah, what does the LORD say He will do?

answers.text: Go down and see if their actions fit the outcry
Wipe out both cities before the sun goes down
Leave the two cities alone until next year

cards.text: Two of the men turn away and head toward Sodom. But Abraham stays right where he is, standing before the LORD.

cards.question: Abraham steps forward to speak to the LORD. What does he ask?

answers.text: Will You really sweep away the righteous with the wicked
Will You really send a warning to the wicked first
Will You really let me walk down with the two men

cards.text: Then Abraham puts a number out there: what if there are fifty righteous people in the city, will the LORD really sweep it away with them in it? Friend, most of us can't even talk our way out of a late fee, and Abraham is making his case to the LORD Himself!

cards.question: Abraham says it would be far from the LORD to treat the righteous and the wicked alike. Then he calls the LORD by a title that fits what he's asking about. What is it?

answers.text: The Judge of all the earth

cards.question: The LORD answers Abraham. If He finds fifty righteous people within the city of Sodom, He will ___ the whole place on their account.

cards.text: Abraham speaks up again, and this time he calls himself nothing but dust and ashes. Friend, I spent YEARS covered in dust in the back of a junk drawer, and Abraham still out-humbled me.

cards.question: Abraham asks what happens if the fifty righteous people are five short. True or false: The LORD says if He finds forty-five there, He will not destroy the city.

cards.text: Abraham asks about forty, and the LORD says on account of the forty He won't do it. Then Abraham says, "May the Lord not be angry…" and he goes down to thirty.

cards.question: True or false: When Abraham asks about thirty righteous people in Sodom, the LORD says thirty isn't enough to spare the city.
After thirty, Abraham speaks to the Lord again and goes lower. What number of righteous people does he ask about next?

cards.text: The LORD answers that on account of the twenty, He will not destroy the city. Fifty. Forty-five. Forty. Thirty. TWENTY. Abraham is counting down like my oven timer, friend!

cards.question: Abraham says, "May the Lord not be angry…" and asks to speak just once more. He asks what if only ___ righteous people are found in Sodom.
The LORD answers that on account of the ten, He will not destroy Sodom. When the LORD has finished speaking with Abraham, what happens?

answers.text: The LORD departs and Abraham returns home
Abraham follows the two men toward Sodom
Abraham asks about five righteous people

cards.text: Keep that apron on, friend. This story is NOT done.
